components.title: Slate desktop application
components.description: Electron desktop notes application with opt-in end-to-end encryption of local data and synced files.
components.purpose: Stores and synchronises notes so that only holders of the user's password, recovery key or device quick-unlock secret can read them.

control-implementations.description: Implementation statements for the fips-140-3 crypto profile of Slate (audit SLATE-CA-2026-10-23).

implemented-requirements.description: In the fips-140-3 profile every cryptographic function protecting notes (AES-256-GCM, AES-256-CTR, HMAC-SHA-256, SHA-256, SP 800-108r1 KBKDF, SP 800-132 PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-512, CTR_DRBG) is invoked through the OpenSSL FIPS Provider 3.1.2 (CMVP #4985) loaded by packages/native with default properties fips=yes. The standard profile uses the same module but includes non-approved Argon2id and is not claimed under SC-13.

Keys are generated by the module DRBG, derived with KBKDF, wrapped with AES-256-GCM and destroyed by handle in the native secure heap; the key inventory with cryptoperiods is docs/compliance/key-inventory.json.
Availability on loss of the password is maintained by a 256-bit recovery key that wraps the master key in a second vault-header slot.
Notes, images and search text at rest are stored only in a SQLCipher 4 database keyed with a per-device 256-bit key; remote copies are SLE2 envelopes.
SQLCipher 4 (AES-256-CBC with HMAC-SHA-512 per page) built against the OpenSSL FIPS provider protects the local database; SLE2 (AES-256-GCM, path-bound AAD) protects every synced file.
All key material lives in the Electron main process inside OpenSSL's mlock'd secure heap; renderers are sandboxed with context isolation and never receive keys.
Key handles are destroyed and verified at lock; the renderer process that held the password is destroyed after unlock; core dumps are disabled with RLIMIT_CORE=0 and PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0 on Linux.

A power-up self-test of the cryptographic module runs at launch: the module loads, the FIPS provider verifies its own integrity and known-answer tests, and an AES-GCM wrap and seal round trip must succeed. A packaged build whose module fails does not start.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Partially implemented. The launch self-test only. The 17-vector self-test with a terminal selftest-failed state, the on-demand run from Settings and the run before every vault change are work package C6 (POA&M POAM-14). This statement is updated when C6 lands.

implemented-requirements.description: Release artifacts and update manifests carry a detached signature verified against a key pinned in the application before an update is applied.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Update artefacts only. Code authentication by the operating system (SI-7(15)) is POA&M POAM-02.

implemented-requirements.description: The power-up self-test verifies the SHA-256 of the FIPS provider binary against a value pinned at build time, and the provider runs its own HMAC-SHA-256 integrity test on load.
In the fips-140-3 profile three failed password attempts within 15 minutes disable password unlock for 180 minutes; the recovery key acts as the administrator release.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Parameter values (3 attempts, 15 minutes, 180 minutes) follow the FedRAMP Rev5 High baseline as recorded in audit section 4.1; the pinned consolidated rules do not carry them (POA&M POAM-13). The throttle is a user-interface control: against someone holding a copy of the data folder the password KDF cost is the cryptographic control.

implemented-requirements.description: In the fips-140-3 profile Slate locks after at most 15 minutes without input, on system sleep and on screen lock; the lock screen hides all note content.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Parameter value (15 minutes) as for AC-7 (POA&M POAM-13).

implemented-requirements.description: In the fips-140-3 profile passwords are at least 15 characters, checked against a bundled blocklist, normalised to NFC and conditioned with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-512 (SP 800-132) with at least 600,000 iterations.

The updater refuses any package whose detached signature does not verify against the pinned release key. The operating system does not authenticate Slate's own code: the macOS build is not notarised and the Linux packages carry no package signature.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Partially implemented. POA&M POAM-01 (no Developer ID or Linux package-signing key, decision D-1) in docs/compliance/poam.md.

implemented-requirements.description: Note content is sealed (SLE1 or SLE2, AES-256-GCM with a path-bound AAD) before it reaches any transport, so what a sync folder, git remote or OneDrive holds is ciphertext.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Transport TLS (git TLS or SSH, and Electron fetch for Microsoft Graph) is outside the validated boundary: accepted risk F-NIST-10, POA&M POAM-11 in docs/compliance/poam.md. OAuth tokens and git credentials depend on those stacks.

implemented-requirements.description: Confidentiality and integrity of note content in transit are provided by the envelope inside the validated module, independent of the transport.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Holds for note content only; credentials are not covered (POA&M POAM-11).

components.title: OpenSSL FIPS Provider 3.1.2
components.description: FIPS 140-3 validated software cryptographic module loaded by packages/native (slate_native.node).
